records.name: Philadelphia Athletics Youth Sports Association (PAYSA)
records.summary: An all-volunteer youth baseball league with five age divisions, from 3 year olds to 12 year olds. Its fall 2026 in-house season is underway, and volunteers coach, umpire and keep the fields up.
records.what_you_do: Kids play weekly practices and Friday or Saturday games. Adults can coach, umpire, help maintain the fields or raise money, after a background check.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 in-house baseball: practices began in late August, games run on Friday evenings or Saturdays, and games are scheduled through November 1, 2026. The age cutoff is May 1.

locations.label: Fields at the 48th and Woodland Avenue Recreation Center

cost.text: The registration fee is not shown on the page. The league says it will not turn away a family who cannot pay the full fee, if the family contacts it before registering.

first_step.how: The fall 2026 sign-up deadline was August 15. Email the commissioner to ask about the next season or fee help, and check the site for the next sign-up link.
first_step.basis: Any child in the age divisions can sign up through a public form each season, though nothing on the page is newcomer specific.

records.notes: Volunteer checks: a Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report, a child abuse history certification, online Safe Sport training and a volunteer disclosure form. An FBI fingerprint check (about $27) is needed unless the volunteer is exempt. These apply to adult volunteers, not to kids. Division ages: PeeWee 3 to 4, TeeBall 5 to 6, Rookie 7 to 8, Minors 9 to 10, Majors 11 to 12. Coach meetings were still to be set. The page names the 48th and Woodland recreation center as the field location.

records.name: Philadelphia Boys and Girls Gymnastics
records.summary: A gymnastics school with preschool classes, beginner girls classes and a boys program that trains toward USA Gymnastics competition. New families can book a free trial lesson before they join.
records.what_you_do: Kids take gymnastics in sessions across fall, winter and spring. Boys who want to compete train in the men's development program. New students fill out an application and a medical form.

schedule.text: Fall, winter and spring classes were announced for enrollment on August 3, 2026. Class days and times are not published on the site.

locations.label: Gym at 3500 Scotts Lane, Suite 2 (WareSpace building)

cost.text: Tuition is not shown on the site. The site links to a summer tuition policy but does not give the amounts. A free trial lesson is offered.

first_step.how: Contact the gym to arrange a free trial lesson, then fill out the application and medical liability forms, or register online for a class session.
first_step.basis: The site offers beginner girls classes and a free trial lesson, and it explains how to start.

records.notes: The boys program is for ages 5 to 18 according to the site's news item. Ages for preschool and beginner girls are not stated. Class days and times are not published. The footer reads 2025, but the August 3, 2026 news item is newer. An older page listed East Falls as the location, so the current Scotts Lane address is used. The site mentions a partnership with Temple University men's gymnastics with no details. No volunteer roles are published. Gymnastics has no exact tag in the vocabulary, so youth coaching and strength training were chosen as the closest fit.

records.name: Philadelphia Outward Bound School
records.summary: An outdoor learning school. Its school and youth group programs serve students in grades 6 to 12, and it also runs day programs, multi-day expeditions and scholarship courses.
records.what_you_do: Schools and youth groups book day programs and expeditions. The site lists scholarship courses without details, and it lists staff openings on its careers page.

schedule.text: Day programs and expeditions are booked by schools and youth groups. Dates, days and times are not published on the page.

locations.label: Philadelphia Outward Bound School, 3401 Reservoir Drive

cost.text: Program costs are not published on the page. Scholarship courses are listed with no details on who qualifies or what they cost.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page and choose program inquiries (for schools and youth groups) or general inquiries, or call 215.232.9130.

records.notes: The directory link outwardboundphiladelphia.org redirects to the national site's Philadelphia page, which is what was read here. Status is probably_active: the only 2026 item is a navigation link named POBS Jamboree 2026, with no month and no dated news. Staff hiring is on the careers page; volunteer roles and background checks are not described. This is a school and youth group program more than a sports program, so the owner may want to decide whether it belongs in sports results.

records.name: Philly Pump Track
records.summary: A bike pump track in West Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, where riders practice on a looping course. It runs weekly dig nights and lists a summer camp and 5 and Under days.
records.what_you_do: Ride when the track is open, after signing the waiver on arrival (a parent or guardian signs for riders under 18). Volunteers can join dig nights, where gloves and tools are provided.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, noon to 6 pm, weather permitting. Dig nights are most Wednesday nights. The season runs from May to late October. The hours and dig night text carries no date.

locations.label: Parkside Avenue, next to the Parkside Evans playground, West Fairmount Park

cost.text: Track entry fees and camp prices are not shown. The camp has a reduced rate for Medicaid-eligible families.

first_step.how: Visit during open hours and sign the waiver on arrival, or download it ahead of time. Under 18s need a parent or guardian to sign.
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a waiver at the track, but the site says nothing more specific about newcomers.

records.notes: Status is dormant under the two year rule. The newest year written on the site is the 2024 season, which opened May 18, 2024. The hours and dig night text is undated and may be current, so recheck before trusting this status. The camp posts (July 17 to 21) carry no year. The footer says 2026, which does not count as evidence. Read from the home page, including Instagram posts embedded on it. No street address, phone or email is published.

notes: Scope: the slice has 30 entries. The Midrange and Morris Athletic Association share one Instagram link, so they are one lead. Verdicts: 18 publish, 1 hide (Power Forward Foundation, a grantmaking body), 1 not_a_group (Rugbee, a fundraising vendor), 3 out_of_area (Southwest Outlaws, Sow Good Now, Will Trippley Foundation). Four are blocked or unreadable (Philadelphia Area Disc Alliance, Philadelphia Dragons, Ralph Brooks, United Philly Soccer). Four are leads only. Searches: both of the 2 allowed were used, and both were for moved or unreadable links (Philadelphia City Soccer Club and Ralph Brooks). Fetches: 39 of 60, including redirects and retries. No broad rate limiting was seen. The Outward Bound and Skateboard Academy directory links redirected to other hosts, and the redirect targets were read because they are the same organizations' own pages. Held back for missing audience.open_to (enrollment is not described on the page, so it was not guessed): Safe-Hub Philadelphia, Skilladelphia, SquashSmarts and The On Deck Circle. Reviewer should check these four first. Status calls to check: Philly Pump Track is dormant because its newest dated text is the 2024 season, though its hours read as current. Dropped leads with reasons: Evolutions Behavioral (a clinical therapy provider, not a community group), Macron (a sponsor), USA Youth and High School Rugby (a national program with no Philadelphia or Pennsylvania program named), and the Ralph Brooks Alumni League (an adult 30 and older league, not youth). The PYSC directory page at pysc.org/community-of-practice/ has no pagination, lists about 150 entries, and many entries have no link. The PYSC homepage shows 12 logos that link to #.
